I am a software engineer and a PhD student in neuromorphic computing at the
University of York, where I study the robustness of spiking neural networks,
training them with PyTorch on cloud GPUs. Before that, I spent two years at
Amazon Web Services on Firecracker, the open-source Rust virtual machine monitor
behind AWS Lambda and Fargate, and became a gatekeeper of rust-vmm, the
virtualisation components shared by Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor and other
virtual machine monitors.

\section*{Experience}

\entry{https://www.york.ac.uk/physics-engineering-technology/}{University of York}{April 2025 -- present}{PhD Student in Neuromorphic Computing, supervised by Prof.~Martin Trefzer}
Research into whether spiking neural networks are more robust than non-spiking
networks, and if so how and why, measuring robustness as a profile across kinds
of perturbation and tracing it to the networks' mechanisms: the reset, the leak
and recurrent connections.
\begin{itemize}
\item Designed an ablation of the leak and the spiking reset, which parallel
  spiking neurons remove so that every timestep can be computed at once by a
  parallel scan, with the outcome on a modular-counting task predicted in
  advance from expressivity results for linear recurrences.
\item Found that a feedforward network with neither a leak nor a reset loses 42
  points of accuracy on Spiking Heidelberg Digits and sends about three times as
  many spikes, and that a leak recovers that accuracy.
\item Compared the networks at equal clean accuracy across the full range of five
  spike perturbations: the reset protects against perturbations that move spikes
  only when the leak is removed, and the leak, rather than the reset, appears to
  decide what a network keeps.
\item Built the experiment pipeline in Python and PyTorch: training and
  evaluation captured as CUDA graphs, training on short-lived fleets of up to
  dozens of cloud GPUs, Bayesian optimisation (Ax and BoTorch) over
  hyperparameters and network topologies, and sweeps that evaluate dozens of
  networks on one GPU at once, analysed with paired bootstrap confidence bands
  and mixed-effects models.
\end{itemize}

\entry{https://aws.amazon.com/}{Amazon Web Services}{April 2022 -- June 2024}{Software Development Engineer, Firecracker, Cambridge, UK}
\href{https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker}{Firecracker} is the
open-source virtual machine monitor, written in Rust, that AWS developed for
serverless services such as Lambda and Fargate.
\begin{itemize}
\item Reworked Firecracker's CPUID handling around the separate Intel and AMD
  specifications, replacing the filtering of host values with a normalisation of
  what each guest is shown; this laid the groundwork for the custom CPU
  templates released in Firecracker 1.4, which let users adjust the processor
  features exposed to a guest.
\item Wrote CPUID compatibility checks for Intel hosts, so that snapshots
  restore safely across hosts.
\item Updated Firecracker's host-security recommendations for Spectre-like
  side-channel attacks, with a test of a host's mitigations.
\item Led an initiative to test Firecracker's performance in production-like
  conditions, coordinating across teams to build the test environment; it found
  significant performance regressions, which were fixed before they reached
  production.
\item Added source-level tracing, released in Firecracker 1.6: a Rust procedural
  macro that instruments functions, and
  \href{https://github.com/JonathanWoollett-Light/clippy-tracing}{clippy-tracing},
  a tool that adds, removes and checks this instrumentation across the codebase.
\item Took on maintenance of \href{https://github.com/rust-vmm}{rust-vmm} and
  became one of its gatekeepers, who administer all of its repositories; wrote
  its guide to handling security vulnerability disclosures, updated its CVE
  management process and started its move to a monorepo.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Projects}

\projectplain{formal}
(2024--present): a parallel explicit-state model checker, written in Rust, for
the RISC-V assembly that existing compilers emit. It accepts a program only if
it can prove, by symbolically executing it across every interleaving of
hardware threads, that no assertion can fail and no memory access is out of
bounds. It verifies a program as written, reporting what the search
established, such as unreachable code and the bytes accessed, and verifies C
compiled by GCC, including multithreaded SV-COMP tasks such as Peterson's and Dekker's locks.
The aim is a paper showing that it outperforms existing checkers on SV-COMP
concurrency tasks, and that an AI agent builds verified software better with it
than with Rust, Dafny, Verus or Lean.

\project{https://github.com/ci-metrics/example}{CI Metrics}
(2023--2024): a prototype of a service, similar to Codecov, that tracks metrics
produced in continuous integration, such as benchmark timings, and reports how each pull
request changes it, prompted by the performance testing of Firecracker. A Rust
backend (Axum, MongoDB), a GitHub Actions integration and a Rust SDK, with
experiments in anomaly detection for flagging regressions in noisy measurements.

\project{https://github.com/nix-rust/nix}{nix}
(2022--2023): contributions to the Rust bindings to Unix system interfaces,
chiefly typed wrappers for epoll and eventfd and the move of several system
calls to Rust's I/O-safety model.

\project{https://byrig.uk/}{Property search}
(2026): a rental-search page that reads floor area from floorplan images with
the Moondream2 vision-language model, running in the browser through
Transformers.js and WebGPU, and ranks listings by weighted preferences,
including a subjective score estimated from pairwise votes with the Glicko-2
rating system.

\projectplain{Neural networks from first principles}
(2020--2024): \href{https://github.com/JonathanWoollett-Light/rust-ad}{rust-ad},
an early prototype that generates forward- and reverse-mode derivatives of
straight-line Rust functions at compile time, and an
\href{https://www.youtube.com/@alittlemorethananintroduct1604}{animated video
series} deriving the mathematics of neural networks.

\projectplain{Hearts of Iron IV modding}
(2024--present): creator of
\href{https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3342313594}{The Think Tank}
and
\href{https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3798403425}{Rising Tide},

\projectplain{Genetic Draughts AI}
(2017): my first venture into machine learning and optimisation, a C++ program

evaluation function evolved through tournaments between candidate players. I
still remember the moment it beat me.
